turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come in, Mr. Iyer, don't hover at the door. Headaches are on the file, but you asked for an early slot, so something has shifted.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes doctor. The pain is there, but it is different now, and I don't know how to explain it properly.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Different how? One side or both?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Mornings are the bad part. I wake up and it is already heavy, both sides, behind the eyes. Not the old one.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): The old headache, still coming?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, still. Five years... well, five-ish years. Left side, it builds, then by night it is gone. That pattern I know.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Is this morning pain throbbing?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Work is mad, doctor, quarter closing, laptop till ten, my manager shouts on the call. I cannot focus.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): I asked about vomiting, not the manager. Any vomiting?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I don't vomit. My headaches are not that type.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): When did the morning ones start?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. Some weeks. Could be a month. I cannot put a date, honestly.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any fever?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, last night the match went late, so sleep was little, and I took two Crocin, those white ones.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Fever. Yes or no?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever. Not hot, not shivering.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Neck stiff?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Neck is fine, I can look down.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Weakness of an arm or leg, or the face pulled to one side?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing like that. I don't know, doctor, I even checked the mirror, the face is the same.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Double vision? Vision blacking out?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): No. With the old left-sided one, light bothers me. This morning pain, light is okay.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Which tablets are you actually swallowing?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Crocin, the white headache tablet, five hundred milligram, quite often. And sumatriptan when the one-sided attack comes.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sumatriptan, what strength, and how many in a week?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): I think fifty milligram, two or three times in a week. Maybe. The strip is at home, I get confused with the box.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): And the Crocin, how many in a day?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Some days three tablets, some days none. I don't keep a count, doctor. I really don't know.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sugar tablets? Blood pressure tablets?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): No sugar tablets for me. My wife takes the water tablet, that is hers, for swelling. I don't take it.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Drug allergy?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. No. I had penicillin years back, no rash, nothing happened.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Snoring? Sleepy in the daytime? Your wife rang the desk.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): She says I snore like anything and I look tired all day. I am not tired, and I don't snore. She exaggerates only. I sleep, that is all.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Past surgery, or a head injury?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): No operation ever. No head injury. A cycle fall when I was small, but that was nothing, I got up and played.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mother or father, migraine? Fits? Brain tumour?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Mother had migraine, bad ones. Father I don't know, doctor, he is no more, nobody told me about tumour or fits.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): You were sure about no vomiting. Still sure?
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, actually, no. Sorry. Two mornings last week I threw up, early, sour, and after that the head pain eased a bit. I forgot just now.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): Morning pain and vomiting, I don't sit on that. I am booking a CT brain for today. You go to radiology from this room.

[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Today itself? I have a client at four. Also, doctor, the sumatriptan still cuts the old left-sided pain in about an hour. Crocin only blunts these morning ones, it doesn't finish them.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): Look straight. Pupils are equal and reacting. Discs are flat, I don't see any swelling.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): That light is strong, but I can see your finger, no double.
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): Chin down to the chest. Neck is soft, no stiffness. Power is full in the arms and legs, and there is no arm drift.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): See, I told you the hands are okay. Is all this for a scan only?
[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): Pulse is seventy-six. Blood pressure is one-twenty-eight over eighty-two. Both are fine.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): One-twenty-eight, is that too much? I don't know these numbers, doctor.
[SEG0049] person_1 (DOCTOR): Not high. I am changing the plan, so today's CT is cancelled. Exam is clean and the vomiting was only two mornings.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): So no scan? Then what, I just go home?

[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): It may be the old headache pattern changing, and I cannot rule out a pressure problem. Come back in two weeks. If the morning headache with vomiting is still happening then, I will order an MRI brain, not a CT.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks I can manage. If I vomit every day before that?

[SEG0053] person_1 (DOCTOR): Then don't wait. Come the same day, or to emergency if the pain is explosive, or if an arm goes weak or vision doubles. Till then, don't take more than three Crocin of five hundred in a day, and keep sumatriptan for the one-sided attacks only, two or three a week as you are, not daily.
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay doctor. The water tablet I should not start, no? My wife offered.
[SEG0055] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do not take her water tablet. It is not yours. Write the morning pain and any vomit on a paper and bring it in two weeks.
[SEG0056] person_2 (PATIENT): I will try. I don't know if I will remember every day, but I will bring something.

spec.situation: Person with long headaches who now has a different pattern (worse in the morning, or with vomiting); takes sumatriptan or paracetamol often; partner says snoring and tiredness too; patient dismisses it. Doctor does a quick neuro exam and orders a scan conditionally.
features: colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.
doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.

spoken_numbers: doses, vitals and durations are spoken as words or sloppy speech ('a hundred and two point five', 'one-forty over ninety', 'five-ish years', 'twenty milligram'); the label writes them normally (102.5, 140/90, 20 mg) and does not turn vague ones into exact ones.
patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.

bad.reason: He denies head injury but mentions a childhood cycle fall; absolute absence is overstated.
Current use for one-sided headache 2-3 weekly is supported; 50 mg dose is uncertain, not definite.
bad.text: sumatriptan (dose=50 mg, frequency=2 to 3 times a week, indication=one-sided headache, status=currently_used, reported_by=patient)

bad.reason: Same-day review is only if vomiting occurs before follow-up, not specifically if it becomes daily.
bad.text: Come the same day if vomiting becomes daily, or go to emergency if the pain is explosive, an arm becomes weak, or vision doubles (action_type=counselling, status=recommended, responsible_person=patient)

omissions.text: The patient first denied vomiting, then corrected this later: initial denial of vomiting was revised to two early-morning vomits last week with some relief of the headache afterward.
The morning headache is present on waking in the morning and is bilateral behind the eyes; this is explicitly stated as different from the old headache pattern.
The old headache is described as not the same as the new morning pain, with the old pattern being familiar to the patient.
No diabetes medication and no blood pressure medication are being taken.
Past penicillin exposure caused no rash or reaction, supporting no known drug allergy.
There is disagreement about snoring/daytime sleepiness: the doctor reports the wife called saying he snores and is sleepy in the daytime, while the patient denies both and says she exaggerates.
Family history also includes no known history of tumour or fits in the father/family, though the patient is uncertain about the father because he is deceased.
Vomiting was described as sour and the headache eased a bit after vomiting.
A CT brain was initially booked for the same day, with instructions to go to radiology from the room.
The same-day CT plan was then cancelled because the examination was clean and vomiting had occurred only on two mornings.
On examination, the optic discs were flat and there was no swelling seen.
Patient-reported during exam: no double vision when following the doctor's finger.
On examination, the neck was soft as well as having no stiffness.
